name: African Women’s Development Fund (AWDF)
summary: A pan-African feminist fund supporting women-led and gender-diverse-led movements. Its latest advertised call is closed; grant types have distinct criteria.

programs.name: Inua Grants — 2025 cycle

geography.scope: Registered and working in Africa; applicant headquarters must be in Africa. Direct transfers to Sudan and South Sudan are restricted.

requirements: African women-led; director and board chair female or gender-diverse; at least 70% female or gender-diverse staff and board.
Inua requires registration.

award.note: 2025 FAQ capped requests at 50% of prior-year income; no absolute range established.

application.note: Current grants page explicitly states the 2025 call closed.

evidence.note: Latest call is closed.
2025 FAQ defines Inua, leadership rules, registration, transfer limitations, income cap and dates.

unknowns: Whether Inua permits sponsorship beyond the stated Sudan/South Sudan transfer workaround

researchNotes: The 2025 call-specific FAQ supersedes older generic three-year registration guidance; no general eligibility claim is extended to other AWDF grant types.

name: AmplifyChange
summary: Supports grassroots advocacy for sexual and reproductive health and rights. The Opportunity Grant page currently schedules reopening for 2028.

programs.name: Opportunity Grants
focus: Sexual and reproductive health rights advocacy

geography.scope: Both organisation and project must be in a listed eligible country.

requirements: Average expenditure over previous two years below GBP 200,000.
Evidence of expenditure required.

award.note: Published program maximum; duration 18–36 months. Next opening is 2028, not an active application window.

application.note: Page says opens in 2028; exact opening and closing dates absent.

evidence.note: Official program page lists countries, expenditure limit, sponsorship pathway, amount, duration and 2028 reopening.

unknowns: Whether published amount changes before reopening

name: Disability Rights Fund
summary: Funds disability-led rights advocacy, including intersectional work. The advertised 2026 intake has elapsed deadlines despite retaining an open-call heading.

programs.name: 2026 Letters of Interest

geography.scope: 2026 call: sub-Saharan Africa, South/Southeast Asia and Pacific Island countries. General FAQ additionally names Haiti; confirm applicability.

requirements: Majority disability/family-member staff, volunteers and/or board.
Sponsor documents and signed agreement required.
Coalitions must have a majority of OPD members and an OPD lead applicant.
Regional grants require regional-level registration and active work in more than three countries.

award.note: Most awards made in 2026 below USD 50,000 for 12 months; this is not a confirmed ceiling for projects starting 2027.

application.note: LOI deadline elapsed; invited full applications due 23 August 2026. Page still says open. Decisions December; projects start January 2027.

evidence.note: Grantseeker guidance contains dates, OPD definition, sponsorship and excluded activities.

unknowns: General operating support has additional track-record and repeat-grantee requirements; it is not available to every applicant.

researchNotes: Closed describes the elapsed 2026 intake, not termination of the fund. The retained open heading conflicts with dated deadlines. Current guidance rechecked October15. Named Mid-level and National Coalition tiers are not offered for the2026 round; the closed2026 call takes priority over legacy policy pages. DRAF shares application information through DRF but remains a distinct directory entity.

name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (UAF-Africa)
summary: Provides rapid funding for unanticipated, urgent opportunities to advance women’s rights in Africa. It also operates protection and advocacy grant routes.

geography.scope: African-based organisations intervening in African countries.

requirements: Women-led, at least 70% women members.
Unregistered groups need a registered sponsor.
Action must be unforeseen, strategic, supported and urgent.

award.note: Rapid Response ceiling; actions within three months. Other grant types have different limits.

application.note: FAQ accepts applications year-round with no funding cycle.

evidence.note: FAQ states year-round access, African local base, sponsorship, leadership, ceiling and exclusions.
Rapid response actions must occur within three months and meet strategic urgency criteria.

name: ELRHA (Enhancing Learning & Research for Humanitarian Assistance)
summary: Supports research and innovation that improves humanitarian outcomes. Its responsive health research mechanism opens only when activated for an exceptional emergency and is currently closed.

programs.name: R2HC Responsive Research Mechanism
focus: Public health research in humanitarian crises

geography.scope: Humanitarian settings; general guidance excludes non-DAC ODA-recipient countries. Call-specific restrictions apply.
exclusions: General vulnerable populations without a qualifying humanitarian crisis

requirements: Project must be humanitarian research; eligibility defined in each activated call.

application.note: Mechanism page explicitly says closed; details follow activation for a particular emergency.

evidence.note: Mechanism responds to exceptional health emergencies; funding is to be confirmed and call is closed.
General guidance defines qualifying humanitarian settings and requires call-specific eligibility checks.

researchNotes: One specific program is researched; this is not a claim that every Elrha funding opportunity is closed. Directory regions remain broad discovery metadata.

name: Tewa – Nepal Women’s Fund
summary: Nepal’s women’s fund supports grassroots organising, feminist leadership, rights and organisational resilience through several grant categories.

geography.scope: Tewa describes support for women’s groups across Nepal.

requirements: Early-stage groups responding to needs of community women.

application.note: Grant documents page provides proposal formats; current intake dates and submission process not confirmed.

evidence.note: Samman supports early grassroots women’s organisations; Tewa operates across Nepal.
Official proposal forms are published, but no cycle or deadline is stated in retrieved text.

researchNotes: Avoided using founder history’s 1990s grant ceilings or registration rules as current policy. Download buttons did not expose document URLs in the parsed page.

name: Women’s Fund Asia (WFA)
summary: Provides flexible support for feminist leadership and rights across Asia. Its Strengthening Feminist Movements programme is awaiting its next call.

programs.name: Strengthening Feminist Movements

geography.scope: Countries listed in the published SFM FAQ; confirm again when the next call opens.

requirements: Self-led rights work at local, subnational or national level.
Published FAQ: budget no more than USD 100,000; legal ability to receive foreign funding.

award.note: Published prior-cycle FAQ: individuals up to 8,000/one year; organisations up to 15,000/one year or 30,000/two years for eligible former partners.

application.note: Program page asks visitors to await upcoming call; overview marks it closed.

evidence.note: Program describes flexible core grants and upcoming call.
FAQ gives prior-cycle locations, budget/leadership rules and category-specific limits.
Programme overview explicitly marks SFM closed.

unknowns: Next call dates and revised requirements
Work-location rules distinct from applicant location

researchNotes: FAQ contains old-cycle references; award and country information are provisional historical criteria. No future opening date invented.

name: Doria Feminist Fund
summary: Funds feminist collectives in the Middle East and North Africa, prioritising new and underfunded women-led and trans-led groups.

geography.scope: Groups based in, or working across, the 20 MENA countries explicitly listed in the FAQ.

requirements: Women-led or trans-led collective work; registered and unregistered groups accepted.

application.note: Official homepage currently advertises open call. Full date/year and timezone not verified.

evidence.note: FAQ lists countries and accepts unregistered groups but excludes individual applications.
Open calls offer core, project and knowledge-production grants.
Homepage advertises applications open and links the official portal.
Groups must be based in OR work across an eligible MENA country. Both base and work must be outside the list before this check can flag a conflict.

researchNotes: Homepage social feed mentions 19 October without a verified year/timezone; deliberately not converted into a machine deadline. Safe transfers for unregistered groups do not establish fiscal sponsorship policy.

name: Samdhana Institute
summary: Supports Indigenous peoples and local communities in Southeast Asia through flexible grants, adviser relationships and capacity support for social and environmental justice.

programs.name: Small grants for grassroots environmental action

geography.scope: The current grants page prioritizes the Southeast Asian social and environmental movement, with support elsewhere as necessary. Southeast Asia is a priority, not a hard exclusion.

requirements: Proposal, group profile and basic management/finance assessment; adviser review.

award.note: Small-grant category in guide and 2024–2025 project; no current 2026 offer confirmed.

application.note: Guide describes adviser-supported proposals, including unsolicited approaches in Philippines/Lower Mekong; confirm current local route.

supported: Community resilience and social justice initiatives

evidence.note: Guide details adviser review and regional operations.
2024–2025 project lists small grants of USD 10,000–30,000 for resilience and justice.
The current grants page prioritizes the Southeast Asian social and environmental movement, with support elsewhere as necessary. Southeast Asia is a priority, not a hard exclusion.

sources.title: Support for Grassroots Environmental Action in Southeast Asia

researchNotes: Historical operational guidance is not treated as a currently open funding call. Geographic screening follow-up on 2026-10-25: The current grants page prioritizes the Southeast Asian social and environmental movement, with support elsewhere as necessary. Southeast Asia is a priority, not a hard exclusion.

name: African Climate Foundation (ACF)
summary: An African-led climate and development foundation supporting systemic transitions through grants, fiscal hosting and institutional support. Funding is identified proactively.

geography.scope: African energy transitions; foundation has country programmes in Ethiopia, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania and Zambia, not an exhaustive eligibility list.

application.note: ACF identifies grants itself and does not accept unsolicited grant proposals.

evidence.note: Programme supports renewable access, planning and investment conditions.
Contact page explicitly excludes unsolicited grant proposals.
African-led climate/development foundation with six named country programmes.

researchNotes: Fiscal hosting as a foundation service is not assumed to mean every externally sponsored applicant is eligible. Named operational countries are not a closed eligibility set.

name: Azim Premji Foundation
summary: Provides multi-year support to nonprofit organisations working with vulnerable communities in India, from early-stage groups to mature institutions.

programs.name: Grants to not-for-profit organisations

geography.scope: Grantwork describes Indian states and locally based teams; applicant registration requirements need confirmation.

requirements: NGO registration form creates access to grant portal.

award.note: Portfolio grants span 1–10 years, usually 3–4; amounts described broadly as lakhs to tens of crores, not an actionable fixed offer.

application.note: Official page accepts NGO registration and provides portal access; no published deadline found.

evidence.note: Multi-year nonprofit grants with registration-to-portal application route.
Grantwork describes themes, Indian states, organisation stages and portfolio duration.

unknowns: Eligible legal forms and fiscal sponsorship

name: Tara Climate Foundation (Tara)
summary: Supports Asia’s clean energy transition through grantmaking and partnerships, including research, policy dialogue and protections for affected workers and communities.

geography.scope: Asia; no exhaustive eligible-country list established.

application.note: Tara does not accept unsolicited grant applications or requests; opportunities are identified with partners.

evidence.note: Programme describes equitable transition research, dialogue and workforce/entrepreneurship support.
Contact page rules out unsolicited funding requests.

name: Aga Khan Foundation
summary: Works through development partnerships and local civil society. A documented JUNTOS! grant cohort in Mozambique supports community-led innovation and organisational resilience.

geography.scope: This documented JUNTOS! cohort concerns Mozambican CSOs, not the full AKF global portfolio.

requirements: Projects co-created with communities through participatory workshops.

application.note: Article records 10 grants awarded July 2025; it is not a current application notice.

evidence.note: Official July 2025 announcement details JUNTOS! grants and community participation.

researchNotes: One concrete subprogramme is represented; do not narrow the entire foundation to Mozambique. An indexed UK annual-report policy was found but its PDF returned 404, so it is not used as decisive evidence.

name: TrustAfrica
summary: Supports African civil society through proactive, collaborative grantmaking and technical support focused on democratic governance, equitable development and African agency.

geography.scope: African civil society; historical grants in 34 countries do not define an exhaustive eligibility list.

application.note: TrustAfrica identifies institutions and plans collaboratively; unsolicited proposals excluded.

evidence.note: Grantmaking policy describes African civil society, proactive selection and exclusions.

researchNotes: Policy also links calls for proposals; any specific advertised call may have its own route. No annual aggregate grantmaking total is treated as an individual award.

name: XOESE – Le Fonds pour les Femmes Francophones
summary: A Francophone women’s fund supporting women-led collective action. Its documented fifth cycle funded feminist rights initiatives; current intake remains unconfirmed.

programs.name: Fifth grant cycle — 2022 call

geography.scope: This historical call covered Francophone countries in Africa and Oceania, and Haiti.

requirements: Women-led collective work; annual budget no more than EUR 200,000 in this cycle.

award.note: Cycle 5 projects in 2023–2024, lasting 3–20 months; EUR 20,000 reserved for multi-year and/or collaborative work.

application.note: Published concept-note deadline elapsed. General policy uses calls and invitations; no new intake verified.

excluded: Workshop participant per diems, food and transport

evidence.note: Official fifth-cycle notice provides eligibility, exclusions, amounts and deadline.
General grant page describes calls and invited partnership proposals.

unknowns: Exact countries beyond the language/region scope

sources.title: Appel à notes conceptuelles du Fonds XOESE

researchNotes: Official search-index text was available, but direct retrieval returned 502/timeouts during this check. Historical dates and amounts are retained explicitly; no current open status inferred.
